## 2026-10-10 · World v3: Port Westport built as a container port

The owner's plan for the bay (docs/WORLD-V3.md 1.2) has "WR3's container port with cranes". Port Westport (district
26) was built at its gulf place with a straight quay on the West Channel and seven crane spots, but it drew as one grey
slab of warehouse roofs (the harbor style wall to wall). Now it is a container port, as WR3 and the docks concept
(SC4-I) show it:

- **The yard** (`buildContainerPort`, district 26's own pass, called where the quay is built; 216 blocks, 27 masts,
  10 straddle carriers): the harbor style's warehouse slabs in the port's rectangle are cleared - the Westport Freight row (the delivery stop and its neighbour)
  and the junkyard stay - and the ground behind the dock is paved. From the dock back: a 6-tile apron under the cranes'
  back reach, then pairs of 5 x 8-tile blocks of container stacks (three rows of 40 ft boxes, two to four high, every
  box its own colour, an invented line's pale mark on some doors) with a tile between the pair and a 4-tile truck lane
  after it; along the quay, groups of four blocks and a 4-tile cross lane. A block needs a tile of yard all round it,
  so no stack touches a road, a pavement, a building or the water. Light masts stand in the tile between a pair (lit at
  night), straddle carriers are parked in the lanes, and the gate is where a lane meets the pavement with a road just
  past it (the one nearest the stacks' middle: halfway along the yard's east side, onto the avenue there) - a barrier
  across it and a gatehouse beside it - and a chain-link fence runs round the main yard's street sides, open at the gate.
- **The quay:** ship-to-shore gantry cranes on its straight edge - the legs on two crane rails (the dock's outer tile
  and the apron's first), the boom out over the water with the trolley and the spreader on its cables, a box hanging
  from every other one - on five of the seven spots (one is on the curve at the north end, one on Harbor Road's end);
  a container ship (the stern with its bridge and funnel, nine holds of boxes, the bow: 90 tiles) moored along the
  middle of the quay; the dock's bollards as before. The cranes are tall props drawn over what's beneath them (the
  boom over the ship and the water), as the elevated road and the tall props are.
- **Solid:** the stacks (a circle per tile), the cranes' legs, the masts, the straddle carriers, the fence and the
  ship's sides; nothing solid on a road or a pavement (the test checks every one).
- **The art:** art v2 draws them as voxel models (`client/art2/props-transit.js`: `stsCrane`, `containerStack`,
  `straddleCarrier`, `shipSection`; the flood mast and the barrier arm it had) through `statics.js`, plus the cranes'
  rails as flat strips; the classic renderer draws them in code (`client/render/portprops.js`), loaded the first time
  one is drawn so the page's startup code doesn't carry it. The art hash changes; the live world doesn't (its ground
  isn't district 26's: the world hash stays `6b6e16fdef9f`).
- **The picture** (`docs/world-v3-westport.png`): the port reads as a container terminal - the stacks in rows, the
  lanes, the red cranes along the quay, the ship alongside. What's still wrong: the quay is the dock's wooden planks (a
  container quay is concrete), the ship is small beside a 344-tile quay (90 tiles; one berth of several), the corner
  past the quay's curve at the north end is still the old district's grass; in the classic renderer, a boat south of a
  crane draws over its boom (it sorts by where things stand), and a ground chunk baked before the port's module arrived
  lacks its rails and fence until it is baked again (the module is asked for as soon as the city has a port).

Asked (stage 2's plan, 8.3: "the generator at the v3 frame, building today's places at their gulf positions and
sizes"): build every gulf place in **one** generateCity call - each was built alone in the full v3 frame, 8-10 s and
about 650 MB apiece - with today's small islands placed whole, the mainland's land as plain ground with its wild
dressing, and the skeleton's crossings between places listed; measure it; draw the whole world.

What it does (docs/WORLD-V3.md 8.6 has the numbers):
- `generateCity(seed, { world3: true, frame, land: buildLand3(today), today })` builds one CityMap of the v3 frame
  (5040 x 4032): Metro City + Southbank (with the canal), Cedar Isle, Westport with Port Westport, the airport,
  Pelican Key and Northshore at their gulf places and sizes; Gull Harbor, Coral Cay, Paradise Cay, Lighthouse Rock and
  Smuggler's Rock placed whole; the islets and the new rocks and Prison Island as the land has them; the mainland as
  ground by its terrain class (sand on its beaches) with trees, rocks and scrub - no mainland roads yet.

  of its piece - the piece whose picture has today's district there (Metro City's and Cedar Isle's rectangles overlap,
  their districts don't), else the small island whose rectangle holds it; what no piece builds goes off the frame.
  In the generator `PL` is the current piece (`pin` / `unpin`); the lines laid in today's coordinates are placed point
  by point, a point over today's water going with its shore. Hashes read the v3 tile.
- **The roads between places:** today's bridges between today's islands are split where they leave one piece and cut
  at the shore (the Bay Bridge, the Pelican Way, the Westport Beltway's ends); the canal's bridges are laid as in a

  Bridge, Airport and Runway Roads, the Pelican Walk, the West Sea Road) are listed in `m.world3.crossings` for the

## 2026-10-10 · The city worker's code budget: 340 -> 360 KB

Merging wave 12 (the whole v3 world in one build, Port Westport's container yard) put the city worker's code at
341 KB against 340 (`node tools/perf.mjs`). That budget measures the worst case: `client/worldgen.js` together with the
city generator it imports only when it must build the city itself - since this afternoon the page downloads the city
from the server or reads its kept copy, and then the worker loads 5 files, 16 KB. What grew is World v3's: the
placement hooks in the generator's passes (`PL`, `pin` / `unpin`) and the container yard's pass (`buildContainerPort`),
reached only by v3 builds. The budget goes to 360 KB. When the v3 world replaces today's, the v3 code is the
generator, and today's island-at-a-time machinery can go.

## 2026-10-10 · World v3 on the server: `CLA_WORLD=v3`

The owner's engine route (docs/WORLD-V3.md part 8): the server builds the world and the pages fetch it. The whole v3
world builds in one go now (8.6), so the server can run it: behind a setting the live deploy never sets, so it can be
tried locally and in tests. Without the setting nothing changes (the world hash stays `6b6e16fdef9f`).

- **The server** (`CLA_WORLD=v3`, `server/config.js` `world`): `server/index.js` builds World v3's world in place of
  today's - `server/world3.js` `buildWorld3`: today's world, the land of the v3 frame, then
  `generateCity(seed, { world3: true, frame, land, today })`, the generator's v3 modules loaded only then - and runs it
  as it runs today's: the World, the art CDN, the region files. **Up in 25-28 s** (the build 19-22 s: today's 4.3-4.6,
  the land 0.9-1.1, the world 14-16; the cut 2.9-4.8 s); **memory 850-870 MB after the build (peak 920-960), 1.56-1.66 GB
  when it starts listening** (the World's state, and the cut's raw copy held until it's gzipped), **1.16 GB once the
  files are written**. One thing broke: the trains, with no railway (the v3 build doesn't lay it yet) - no trains then.
- **The region files at v3:** 80 regions (10 x 8) and the index, **8.63 MB gzipped** (358 MB raw); regions 34-260 KB
  (median 63 KB; the 9 largest together 2.03 MB). **The index 1.26 MB -> 0.71 MB gzipped** (5.97 -> 2.06 MB raw), the
  format's version 2 (`shared/regionpack.js`; the files are still the city to the bit, less what only the generator
  reads):
  - 84,911 of its references were items of one regional list that are another's (81,745 offshore points that are sea
    points, 2,796 lamps that are props, 104 ATMs that are POIs): each is said in its own region now (a region's `refs`).
  - The railway's points (`railPts`, 14,127 in today's world; none at v3, where it isn't laid) and the levels' deck
    segments (`levels.segs`, by their middle - a list inside a field, by its path) are regional; the levels' grid stays.

## 2026-10-10 · The art after a far teleport; room in the renderer's code

What the last waves found (docs/WORLD-V3.md 8.9's open item 4, 8.12's item 8): "after a far teleport the art v2 view
shows the sea's stand-in for a long time - 40 s and more in the headless page - although the server's art CDN has the
chunks baked and the minimap shows land"; and the renderer's code at 363 of its 363 KB. What was wrong, and fixed
(docs/WORLD-V3.md 8.12.1 has the detail):
- **The server baked each look back to front** (`server/artcdn.js`): a page asks nearest first, the server took asks
  newest first - the chunk under the player came last. Now the latest look (asks within 2 s of the newest) goes first,
  in the order it asked (`askNext`; `askAhead` for the 404's eta).
- **A run of misses paused the page's asking for 15 s, each missed chunk for 30 s** (`client/art2/game/worker.js`
  `fromCdn`): after a teleport every chunk on screen is queued on the server at first, so the asking stopped and the
  page baked everything itself. A 404 with an eta (queued: it's coming) is asked for again about then and doesn't count.
- **The page looked for a chunk in its store and on the server once** (`host.js` `_chunks`): now again every 2.5 s
  while the view needs it; and **just after a jump** (teleport, respawn) up to 4 chunks are uploaded a frame, not 1-2.
- **World v3's window swap** dropped the bakes asked for against the old window (they came back with its walls and sea
  and were drawn) and redraws the stand-ins made from it; the bake worker never keeps a chunk baked against a window's
  walls (`inWindow`) - it could have gone into the browser's store as the real art.

## 2026-10-11 · World v3: the window's signatures, the world's places, the kept regions, the minimap

The page keeps a window of the v3 world (8.12); its follow-ups, as the owner's plan lists them: "per-region
signatures" (part 8 item 5: "the world hash and each region's signature are checked against what was read from the
cache"), the phone's apps and the big map listing the whole world's places ("a small global list (name, kind,
position) belongs in the index"), "regions kept one by one" in the browser, and a coarser minimap at v3.
- **The signatures:** the index carries each region's signature (a hash of its file as written) and the world's (the
  map's, what the welcome says). The city worker's window keeper checks each region as it assembles it: one that
  doesn't match (or doesn't open) is dropped - from memory and from the browser's store - and fetched again past every
  cache; refused again, no window is assembled and the page says which region (the title screen at the start, a
  toast on a move). The welcome's signature is checked against the index's: another build reloads into it, the same
  build reloads once - and that load is afresh (nothing kept read, everything past the HTTP cache: the v3 world's files
  keep their URL while today's world's hash does). Today's world: the whole-map check as before.
- **The world's places:** the index lists every POI (id, kind, label, position, district, home); a window's city
  carries them as `places`, by the POI's world index, and the phone's Places app (the list, the district, the
  waypoint), its nearest courthouse and ATM, the big map's icons and its panel read them - a window lists the whole
  world's places (860 at v3; 339 outside the window round the gulf's hospital). The big map's district names too: each
  district's middle in the index (before, the first window's districts alone).
- **The regions kept in the browser** (IndexedDB `cla-regions`, under the world's hash and the seed): the worker reads
  the index and the window's regions from there and downloads only what it hasn't kept; a new world clears the old
  one's. A return visit downloads nothing it has.
- **The minimap at v3:** a coarse picture of the whole frame in the index (a tile every 4, only for a big frame) and
  the window's own picture over it: 5.1 + 9.1 MB of pixels, not a frame-sized canvas's 81 MB. Today's world: as before.
- What it weighs: at v3 the picture is 51 KB of the index (gzipped), the places 13 KB, the signatures 1 KB; today's
  index 0.359 -> 0.371 MB, its regions byte for byte as before.
- Nothing live changes: today's world keeps its path (its index carries the new lists, unread); the world hash stays
  6b6e16fdef9f; the files' format stays 2 (the new index fields are optional both ways). The page's code 466 -> 467 KB
  of 485; the city worker 33 -> 34 files (client/regionstore.js), 357 KB of 360.

## 2026-10-11 · World v3 on the server and the deploy: measured, the art thread's world, the worker's room, the switch's runbook
The owner's brief: "the live server runs today's world; World v3 runs on a test server with CLA_WORLD=v3 ... Before the
owner can switch, the server and the deploy must carry it. Measure, fix the cheap wins, and write down the rest" - and
"the switch itself, written as a runbook ... No switch is made." All of it in docs/WORLD-V3.md 8.23.
- **Measured** (this machine, two shared cores): the v3 server listens after **50-53 s** (the build 44-45 s - twice
  8.9's, the world has grown), **1.85 GB** at listening (the cut's 384 MB raw held till gzipped); 81 region files,
  13.2 MB gzipped. The tick with 6 players spread over the world: **11.4-12.3 ms** (today's world 7.3-7.6), the
  trains 1.0-1.6 ms of it even with nobody on, wildlife, traffic and EMS the others that grow.
- **The art CDN baked today's world at v3** (found and fixed): its bake thread built its city from the seed - today's
  world - so on a v3 server it baked the sea at nearly every v3 chunk (that was 8.9's "the sea's stand-in" round Port
  Westport and Highland Woods). The thread now builds the world the server runs, and the CDN checks the thread's map
  signature against its own before it bakes anything (another city: no art from the server, the pages bake their own).
  At v3 that costs the thread's own build (45 s of the second core at the lowest priority) and memory: 3.6 GB while it
  builds, 3.2 GB after. 35,280 chunks a quality: about 8-9 hours a quality on the VM's one bake thread. And each art
  directory now says which world it's of (`world.txt`): the build before stands in only when it's the same world's (at
  the switch today's chunks won't stand in for v3's places), and a directory of the shared art hash holding the other
  world's chunks is baked afresh.
- **The whole-world scans:** the traffic's parking spots, bike racks and spawn edges near each player, and the
  ambulances' start junctions, through spatial indexes (`server/pointgrid.js` `near`, `traffic.js` `edgesNear`) -
  the same picks in the same order.
- **The city worker's room:** 358 -> 349 KB of its 360: what only v3 builds reach (Port Westport's container port, the
  main line's loops as one, its hubs, switches and bores) moved verbatim out of `shared/map.js` into
  `shared/world3-passes.js`, registered like the island builds when `shared/world3-islands.js` is imported.
- **The runbook** (8.23): what to build first (the art key per world - the page keeps chunks under one art hash for
  both worlds: play the v3 test server in its own browser profile; version.json's world hash for v3; `LEGACY_HOMES[9]`),
  the `WORLD_VERSION` bump (homes, garages, stashes and bounties: released as World v2 did - the homes bought back at
  their deeds, the cars and stash kept, bounties kept), the art and the region files warmed, the health check's 90 s
  against a 50 s start, and the rollback (profiles that played v3 are world 10: take a backup at the switch).
- **Nothing live changes:** today's world hash `6b6e16fdef9f` and art hash `cdd307a65f3a` unchanged; the indexed
  lookups pick what the loops picked; the art thread builds today's world as before (and posts its signature, the
  same).

## 2026-10-11 · World v3: the land's relief - heights, cliff bands, the hillshade
The v3 land was flat (WORLD-V3.md 8.20 and 8.21: "Silver Thread Falls reads as a weir ... the land has no heights yet",
"Lookout Hill isn't a hill", "North Cape has no headland"; 8.18: "the lookout isn't on the mesa"; 8.8: "the mesas and
buttes read as small red towers"). Now it has relief:
- **A height field for the v3 frame** (`shared/world3-relief.js`, one call from the world build): the peaks high with
  crags, the North Ridge a ridge, the woods' hills, the valley a basin, the desert a plateau; Lookout Hill a hill above
  Kestrel Lake; the headlands (North Cape, Egret Point, Sandpiper Point, Toll Point) high ground ending in cliffs behind
  the beach; the desert's mesas and buttes big raised tables with cliff sides (the lookout's mesa one of them, its jeep
  track the ramp); the gorge under the Gorge Bridge; an escarpment and gorge at each falls (Silver Thread Falls, Summit
  Tarn's). Deterministic: integer hashing, no Math.random.
- **Roads keep their grade:** a road's height is the land's averaged along it; the land beside it comes back over 14
  tiles - cuttings and embankments, never a cliff across a road.
- **Cliff bands where it's steep:** open wild ground steeper than 2.2 m a tile is solid rock with its faces on the south
  rims (granite in the desert and the peaks, basalt elsewhere).
- **Drawn:** the art v2 ground bake shades the ground by the slope and the height (`M.relief`: a hillshade lit from the
  north-west); a desert table's band is red rock. Nothing live changes: the world hash stays 6b6e16fdef9f (the art's
  changes).

## 2026-10-11 · Jobs and the honest living: the job's truck always there and marked, work trucks, the Act prompt, Safety mode, felonies, no cars on home lots (H57)

The owner's notes, in their words: "Delivery jobs that are supposed to give you a flatbed to use don't always seem to
spawn a flatbed for you. If there is a truck or equipment that is spawned for your job you take on, let's make sure it's
visible on screen with a visual indicator like a pulsing circle UI around it"; "Jobs, make arrow in minimap, make clearer
where your job is, arrow for truck you are given. Work trucks you can paint and steal if you want but you can't just park
a work truck in your garage and keep it. You get paid extra for dropping truck off back home."; "Safety citizen mode,
warns you before stealing a car accidentally or other crimes to help you live a good life."; "'Act' on cars will tell you
if you're stealing a car or if it's your own car"; "Stealing a car is a felony? Maybe we tone down the severity of some
less severe crimes"; "Owned player properties have vehicles parked halfway in the garages, shouldn't have vehicles parked
there."
- **The job's truck, always** (`server/systems/jobs.js` `workTruck`): why it went missing - the courier job skipped the
  truck when any free cargo truck stood within 320 px, the spot search gave up at 260 px, and the truck it did park was
  "tidied away like any parked car once nobody is around": a job taken from the phone across town lost its flatbed to the
  despawner before you got there. Now a free flatbed already at the pickup is issued to you (and taken off the parked-car
  spawner's books), otherwise one is parked on open ground searching out to `WORK_TRUCK.searchR` (1,400 px), and the job
  keeps it (`despawnable` false) until the job ends (or its driver leaves the game: `jobs.update` lets it go). The farm's
  co-op flatbed is the same truck. `p.job.truck` is its id.
- **Marked until you're in it**: the job tracker (`phone.jobTarget`) carries `veh` (the truck, while you're not in it) and,
  while you're picking up, `dest` (where the cargo goes after). On screen (`client/main.js` `drawJobTruck`): a green pulsing
  ring and YOUR TRUCK on it and, when it's off screen, a green arrow at the screen's edge pointing to it. The minimap
  (`client/hud.js`): the pickup / job target yellow as before, the destination orange, the truck green - a blip in range,
  an arrow on the rim when not. The world map (`client/worldmap.js`): the truck as a green dot with a car icon; its side
  panel (`client/mapwaypoints.js`) shows your job and how far.
- **Work trucks** (`homes.js` `storeVehicle`, `vehicleInteraction`): drive one, paint it, keep it out - but a garage won't
  keep one (the prompt says so; storing it is refused with why). Once the job's done, bring it back to where it was issued
  for `WORK_TRUCK_RETURN` ($150, `shared/rules.js`): the tracker says "Bonus: bring the Flatbed Work Truck back to ..." and
  points there, and at the spot (within 240 px) Act hands it in (`jobs.truckInteraction`, `returnTruck`); the offer lasts
  15 minutes (`WORK_TRUCK.returnS`), then the company collects it. A job given up: collected (no bonus). Someone else
  taking your company truck is vehicle theft.
- **The Act prompt says what getting in is** (`vehicles.js` `entryInfo`, `enterLabel`; `players.js` `findInteraction`):
  "Get in your Sedan", "Get in the Flatbed Work Truck - issued to you for the job", "Get in your rental ...", "Steal the
  Sedan - Vehicle theft", "Steal the Police Interceptor - Stealing a police vehicle (felony)", "Pull the driver out of the
  Sedan - Carjacking" (and "Violent carjacking (felony)" when it's moving), "Ride along in the ..." (a player's car with a
  free seat). Someone else's crate: "Pick up Wood Box - Cargo theft".
- **Safety mode** (`server/systems/safety.js`; Settings → Safety mode; `store.js`: on for new characters, existing ones
  off until switched on - kept with the character): the first press of an act the game knows is a crime before it
  happens only warns and names it ("Safety mode: that's Vehicle theft - a crime. Press again to do it anyway") - the
  same act again within `SAFETY_CONFIRM_S` (4 s) does it. Covered: getting into a car that isn't yours or pulling a

## 2026-10-11 · Flying: helicopters and light planes (H56)

The owner (2026-10-11): "When will we add the flying mechanic in for helicopters and airplanes? I'd like to see those
come together soon." Later waves build on this: search-and-rescue, coast guard and private-pilot jobs with helicopters
(a harness lowered to people; landing on hospital roofs) and "an attack helicopter you can fly and shoot missiles from,
can spawn in debug".

- **Flight on the server, predicted on the page** (`shared/flight.js` `flightStep`, `flightInput`): an aircraft is a
  vehicle of kind `air` with an altitude (`alt`, px), a climb rate, its engine's spool and (planes) a bank. A
  **helicopter** spools up (3.2 s), lifts off straight up, hovers with nothing pressed, tilts to move - the way the
  stick points, or W/S along the nose with A/D yawing it on a keyboard - and eases its descent near the ground (a flare:
  a full descend still touches down softly). Without power it falls - a crash. A **light plane** taxis on its wheels (the
  nose wheel steers), needs a take-off roll on hard ground to reach its rotate speed (`vr` 520 px/s: a runway, the
  apron, an airstrip's dirt, a long straight road - grass, sand and fields hold it below that), climbs when you pull up
  at flying speed, banks to turn, holds its speed with the stick let go, stalls below 400 px/s (the nose drops, it
  sinks), and rolls out on its wheels. Low down it hits what stands taller than it is: buildings by their height
  (`bldTop`: by district style and size, hospitals 240 px, towers to ~880), walls, trees and solid props below 110 px;
  high enough it flies over them and it can set down on a flat roof.
- **Consequences** (`server/systems/aircraft.js`): a bump hurts it; flying into something faster than 240 px/s, a
  touch-down faster than 330 px/s or ditching at speed is a crash - it blows up where it is (`vehicles.explode`, so
  `explosions.js` and the people thrown clear); between 150 and 330 px/s a hard landing hurts it, and a plane put down
  off the hard ground at speed digs in. Down gently in the water it floats and sinks like a car (everyone swims). Two
  aircraft close in height that touch both come down. Up in the air, ground traffic and people pass under it
  (`airborne`: over 24 px); nobody boards one in the air; getting out: on the ground only - in the air the first press
  warns, the second jumps (hurt by the height, much less into water); not off a roof.
- **Where they are** (`airfields(m)`: computed from the built map - the airports' runways and stands, the Route 9 /
  Dry Creek airstrip, the police HQ, the hospitals - so the generator and the world's hash are unchanged): helipads at
  the airport, the police headquarters and every hospital's yard, and one on each hospital's roof (data for the next
  wave's landings; drawn in the classic renderer only - art v2 stands its buildings up), all kept off the runways and
  taxiways. Parked: a police helicopter at HQ (officers take it freely; anyone else, it's stealing a police vehicle), a
  helicopter at the airport's pad and the first hospital's yard, a light plane by each of the apron's planes and at the
  airstrip; taking one is vehicle theft as for cars; one taken or wrecked comes back to its spot 4 minutes later once

## 2026-10-11 · Fire on people, the explosion tester and the tank (H58)

The owner: "NPCs and players catch on fire if they are near an explosion or their vehicle blows up or they run into
fire. NPCs run for it and either run off screen or run then stop, drop and roll, or they just fall to the ground and burn
to death. If NPCs are near water there's a chance they'll run to the water and jump in to put themselves out. Rain makes
the fire go out faster. Player characters: you want to roll on the ground to put yourself out, running around on fire
makes you go out but a little slower, jumping in water puts you out immediately." - "Explosions debug happens when you
press it in the debug menu but you can't see what's happening on screen because the debug menu is on top. Maybe this
debug should be an item you shoot or something you can trigger while in game so we can test explosions as rapidly as we
had before." - "Add a tank you can drive and shoot and blow things up with, can spawn in debug."

- **Fire on people** (`server/systems/burning.js`; `shared/rules.js` BURN): someone alight has `ped.burnT` (the seconds
  the fire has left, standing still in the dry) and takes BURN.dps a second (a player's grit divides it). What sets
  people alight: a blast (`combat.blast` → `blastCatch`: likelier the nearer its heart), their vehicle blowing up with
  them in it (`vehicles.js` blownOut: thrown clear on fire), a fire arrow (`combat.js` stepArrow), and walking or
  running into fire (checked every few ticks) - a burning vehicle or a fresh wreck, a lit campfire (not sitting by one),
  someone alight brushing past; standing still beside a fire you don't catch, and spawn protection keeps it off.
  It goes out by itself in BURN.secs (9 s), faster running about (x1.6), much faster dive-rolling on the ground (x9: a
  couple of rolls), faster again in the rain (x2.2), and at once in the water (a hiss). Getting into a car or going
  indoors puts it out. A player is told; the death screen says "Burned to death." (or "...set alight by" whoever).
- **Burning NPCs** panic (`burning.js` npcCatch / npcStep; `npc.js` hands them over while `n.burn`): near water (380 px)
  most run for it and jump in; otherwise a third run off as far as they can, a third run a moment and then stop, drop
  and roll (down, rolling side to side, out in 2.4 s), a third stagger a few steps and fall, burning where they lie until
  they die. Cops and medics just burn. Shaken, the ones who put it out run on a while.
- **Seen and heard**: the burn bit rides in the ped record's parent field (its top bit: `net.js`; `main.js` strips it);
  flames lick up the body (along it, lying down) and dark smoke rises - the pooled particles (`render/fx.js`), which both
  renderers draw and art v2 lights; 'ignite' plays a whoomph and a scream, 'scream' every second or two while it burns,
  the ambience's fire crackle follows the nearest one alight, 'douse' hisses.
- **The Boom Tester** (`server/systems/boomtest.js`; `shared/items.js` boomtest, index 29 - the wire's last free weapon
  index): a dev-only weapon in the give menu and the debug menu's new 🔥 section. Its shot flies like a rocket and sets
  off the kind picked where it lands (on what it hits, or at the end of its range): small / medium / big / ultra blasts,
  a car going up (its own plan), launched, blown apart, losing a burning wheel, a fuel tanker, an explosives truck, or a
  burst of fire that sets people alight. The reload key steps through the kinds (BOOM_TEST_KINDS). The debug menu stays
  closed while you test.
- **The tank** (`server/systems/tank.js`; `shared/vehicles.js` tank, index 60 - clear of the fleet's run; `shared/rules.js`
  TANK): on tracks - it turns on the spot and never slides (`shared/physics.js`: def.tracks), mass 14 (it shoves cars
  aside), small arms barely scratch it (def.armor 0.06 in `vehicles.js` damageVehicle), a rocket or a shell takes a sixth
  of it (def.rockets in `combat.blast`), and a chain reaction never sets it off by chance. Its turret turns to the
  driver's aim at 2.4 rad/s on its own (it holds its bearing while the hull turns under it); the fire button sends a
  shell every 1.8 s that flies 900 px and goes up where it lands - a blast that wrecks vehicles like a rocket's (the
  projectile's `land` hook in `combat.js` stepProjectile, shared with the Boom Tester). The turret's angle from the hull
  rides in the vehicle record's damage word's top byte (`tank.turretByte`). Art v2: the hull and the turret are their own

  the breech's clang ('tankfire'). Debug only: the debug menu's 🔥 section spawns one; nobody sells it.

## 2026-10-11 · H59: flying for a living - search and rescue pilot, charter pilot

The owner: "Let's add more jobs for players trying to make an honest living. With helicopters and airplanes being added we
should create citizen jobs you can do with helicopters. Like search and rescue helicopter pilot job: patrol around and
respond to calls of missing or hurt hikers out in nature spots, and you get a general idea where they may be but you
gotta go out and search for them and retrieve them. They're either injured and you have to land and pick them up and
bring them back and fly them to the hospital, which you can land on top of, or you need to lower a harness down to
hard-to-reach places, or find them in the water and lower a harness, or just locate a missing person and pick them up."
And: "Private helicopter pilot for rich billionaire customers flying around the world from location to location."

- **Search and rescue pilot** (`server/systems/sar.js`; `shared/rules.js` SAR): sign on at a hospital's yard helipad (Act
  there) or from the phone (Jobs › Flying). A rescue helicopter - its own model, `rescueheli`, index 64 (the next free
  aircraft index), red and white (the overlay's 'rescue' livery) - is issued to you like a work truck (`v.issuedTo`,
  `v.workTruck`: the ring and the arrows until you're in it, not theft, Safety mode doesn't ask). A shift of calls, one
  after another: someone hurt on open ground, someone hurt and stuck where nothing can land (among the trees and rocks),
  someone in the water off the coast, or someone just lost - out in the wild, rural, park, rocky, beach and desert
  districts or the water near the shore (`sitesOf`: a sweep of the built map, nothing added to it - the world's hash is
  the same). The page gets a search circle (the job target's `area`: drawn on the minimap and, labelled, on the world map)
  with the spot somewhere inside it, not the spot. Within 560 px they see you: they wave (the fist pump's arm up) and a
  smoke flare goes up beside them (`flare`: an orange plume, drawn in both renderers by `client/render/aircraft.js`).
  The hurt and the lost: land within 320 px and they come aboard (the hurt helped by the crew). The stuck and the
  swimmer: hover low right over them and hold Act - the cable pays out (85 px/s) and, once it reaches them, winches
  them up (110 px/s; let go and it holds); higher than 300 px above them, drifting faster than 120 px/s or not over them
  and it can't reach. The cable is drawn on the overlay out of the side door (`hoist`), them hanging in the harness once
  clipped on. A hurt patient's time runs down (260-380 s from the call; a hard landing with them aboard takes 40 s off
  and is counted: `aircraft.js` remembers each touchdown's sink as `v.landSink` / `v.landAt`); if it runs out, they die
  and the call pays nothing. Land on a hospital's roof pad - or the helipad in its yard - to hand them over: $260 + $90 a
  km of the call's distance from the hospital, up to +60% for a quick rescue, less 25% a hard landing (down to 40%), and
  6 Samaritan points. A call nobody reaches in 12 minutes goes to another crew; cancelling the job (the phone) sends the
  helicopter back and whoever was out there is fetched by someone else.
- **The hospitals' roofs are roofs now** (`shared/flight.js` tileTop): the hospitals are walk-in buildings, their insides
  T.FLOOR, so the roof pad over the middle had no roof under it - a helicopter "landing" there sank to the ground inside.
  A walk-in building's floor now counts as under its roof for flying (`floorAt`), so the roof pads work (and you can't
  fly through a shop at roof height any more).
- **Art v2 draws aircraft at their height** (the owner's call, after the first playtest showed a helicopter "on" a
  hospital's roof drawn down on its front wall): art v2 stands everything up - something at a height is drawn that much
  up the screen - and now an aircraft is too, by its altitude times `V2_LIFT` (0.66: a roof's drawn height over its
  flying height, measured on the hospitals' roofs; `client/render/aircraft.js` liftOf), its shadow staying on the ground
  - or on the roof under it. So a helicopter down on a roof sits on the drawn roof, the roof pads are drawn up there (they
  were hidden in v2), and the harness's cable hangs straight down the screen to the one below. The camera follows two thirds of
  the lift of your own aircraft (`main.js`), so you and the ground under you both stay on screen. The classic view is as
  it was. The job's marker points at the hospital's roof pad (the yard's helipad takes them too). Left: the gunship's
  missiles are still drawn at ground level in v2, below the lifted gunship (a projectile carries no height on the wire).
- **Charter pilot** (`server/systems/charter.js`; `shared/rules.js` CHARTER): from the phone (Jobs › Flying) - the company's
  Skylark is issued at the nearest helipad. Bookings one after another: a rich customer (invented names: Sterling
  Vanderholt, Margaux Ellery-Price...) waits at one of the places a helicopter goes - the airport's helipad, the airport's
  apron and the airstrips, a mansion's lawn in each rich district, a landing spot on each island (`placesOf`, from the
  built map) - and wants flying at least 3 km to another, for a board meeting or lunch on the islands. Land within 320 px
  and they board; land within 240 px of the destination and they step out: the fare ($180 + $70 a km) and a tip of up to
  half of it - none after a hard landing, less the more the helicopter is knocked about or shot at on the way, more the
  quicker the flight.
- The phone's job list has a Flying section (`client/phone.js` flyJobs: the jobs marked `fly`); the dev menu's command
  `sar` (`server/dev.js`) signs you on in your rescue helicopter, and with `k` starts a call of that kind at the nearest
  such place (`hover`: hovering over them; `hooked`: them on the cable; `roof`: a patient aboard, down on the nearest
  hospital's roof pad).
- **The coast guard** (`server/systems/coastguard.js`; `shared/rules.js` COAST; the owner: "Coastguard jobs: patrol in
  boats and helicopters to hunt down criminal activity on the water, usually smugglers or traffickers. Do search and rescue
  type missions too"): from the phone (Jobs › Flying), a boat patrol - the orange rescue boat (`rescueboat`, its coast
  guard livery as it is) issued at the nearest harbour on the sea - or an air patrol - a rescue helicopter at the nearest
  helipad. A shift of calls, two in three smugglers:
  - **Smugglers**: a speedboat with two contraband crates aboard - out in the open on its deck, like any cargo - and two
    Syndicate men runs 2.5-5 km along the coast toward Smuggler's Rock (`rescue.js` wayTo plans the way round the land,
    `boats.js` boatSteer drives it). Stay alongside (within 240 px in a boat, or within 320 px across and below 320 px in
    the helicopter) for 4 s and they heave to and put their hands up (shooting the one at the wheel works too). Then
    board them - Act alongside in the boat, or low over them in the helicopter ("a crewman goes down the line"): the
    crates are seized, the crew arrested and the boat impounded: $300 + half the cargo's value, 10 Samaritan points. Lose
    them (5 km off for 25 s), let them make their drop or sink them with the cargo and the call's lost. Running them down
    isn't reckless ramming for the coast guard (`law.js` vehicleRam).
  - **Someone overboard**: a search circle (500 px) where they went in; within 600 px they're found (the flare). In the
    boat, pull alongside, slow, and Act - hauled aboard; in the helicopter the harness, as the rescue pilot's (hold Act
    over them; the page draws the cable). Then ashore - the boat run in slow by dry land, the helicopter landed on dry
    ground - handed to the paramedics: $280, up to half again for a quick rescue.
  - Only the sea: a flood from the open sea's points (m.offshore) over what boats can cross marks the water joined to it,
    so the patrol boat, the smugglers and the calls are never on a lake inland (Lakeview's hire dock was the nearest
    "harbour" in the first playtest). Neither the rescue calls nor the coast guard's are under the elevated highway any
    more (`sar.js` sitesOf skips water and ground within two tiles of `m.deck` - a swimmer under the viaduct in the
    playtest, with the helicopter hovering over the road deck).

  can't measure frames here - the software WebGL draws 0.3-0.5 frames a second, every run alike (helicopter low and
  high, the plane, a sports car) - so the art's demand was measured on the real map instead (the renderer's own
  _prebakeList, a phone's view and the camera's pull-back, a straight run from downtown over the suburbs):
  chunks coming on screen a second - helicopter flat out (720 px/s) 4.0, the plane (1150 px/s) 6.1, a sports car flat
  out 4.3 - and how far ahead each was first put on the list the downloads and the bakes ahead work through. That list
  was a car's: a band three chunks wide along the way you go and the roads from here, which a helicopter crossing the
  blocks doesn't follow. Flying, it's now a band as wide as the view along the way you fly and no roads (host.js
  _prebakeList): chunks listed 2 s or more before they show 76% -> 88% (helicopter), 71% -> 93% (plane), 88% -> 93%
  (flying north), none never listed (was 2-5%), median lead 6.0 -> 8.1 s. And the speed's pull-back (1.5x flat out) is
  held to the flying cap like the height's (1.45x on a phone, easing to 1.1x while chunks on screen are stand-ins; the
  speed's eased only to 1.25x): 4.0 -> 3.9 chunks a second flat out, 3.5 -> 3.2 while late (main.js). Budgets

  helicopter and a plane passing close, then three people alight - the crackle, their screams - with the Boom Tester's
  four blasts and a police siren; and the same with the old street-furniture barrage under you):
  - the soft ceiling is never driven (0% of the samples over its knee) and the compressor barely (3.6 dB at most, in

    you peaks at -17 dBFS (first) / -20 (2f3ba8a) - so the entry above's "drove the mix into its soft ceiling" didn't
    hold up on the bench;

    changed the mix;
  - what was wrong: the rotor's energy was mostly where nobody hears anything - its note at 17-30 Hz and its sub-octave
    at 8-15 Hz: 41% of what came out under 25 Hz (2f3ba8a 28%), which a phone's speaker can't play but still gets
    pushed about by; and the street furniture smashed under you (+6 dB, a crash every 0.6 s). The master now runs

## 2026-10-11 · Gardening at home and farm work: the plots in your yard, the tractor on the fields (H61)

The owner: "Have we added farm jobs and gardening mechanics yet?" - and wants both. There was the harvest contract (haul
4 Produce Boxes in a co-op flatbed), picking at the orchard and the vineyard, and the farms' FIELD tiles. Now:
- **A garden at home** (server/systems/gardening.js). An owned home's yard has a few plots (up to GARDEN.plots), found
  from the built map: two tiles of open yard side by side, a tile in from the lot's edge (the painted lots keep their
  hedges there), clear of the house, its door, its drive and the props, in a bed at the back of the lot - nothing is
  added to the map, the world's hash is the same. 86 of the 115 houses have one (44 with three or more), the cottages,
  farmhouses, beach houses and the mansion too; apartments and shacks none. Seeds (tomato, carrot, lettuce, pumpkin)
  at the farm co-op's counter (Dry Creek's co-op and the Cedar Farms market: SHOPS.farm), the Old Town market and the
  hardware store. At an empty plot of yours the Act button plants the seeds you carry; at a growing one it waters it
  (the rain waters them all). A watering lasts GARDEN.waterDays in-game days; a plant grows only while it's wet, ripe
  after its crop's days of wet growing (GARDEN_CROPS: a day to two and a half - 20 to 50 minutes); dry too long it
  wilts (water perks it up, but a prize is lost) and then dies (clear it and sow again). Picked ripe, its yield goes in
  your bag - eaten it heals, the grocery and the co-op buy it (SHOPS.grocery, SHOPS.farm) - and now and then (10%,
  rolled at planting) it's a prize one worth GARDEN.prizeX times as much. The plots live with the home in the profile
  (prof.garden[homeId]: a home sold, its garden is out of play - kept on the profile, back if you buy it again) and grow while you're away (stepped with the server; what passed
  while it was down is caught up from each garden's wall clock). Someone else can't work your plots; everyone sees them.
- **Farm work** (server/systems/farming.js). The farms' fields (map.fields) are kept on the server in rows FARM.rowW px
  wide along each field's length, each going round stubble -> ploughed -> sown -> growing (FARM.growDays) -> ripe ->
  harvested. Driving a tractor down a row does the job it needs once FARM.cover of it (in FARM.segs stretches on field
  tiles) has been driven over; the stretches done show behind the tractor. The tractor is vehicle 48 (shared/vehicles.js:
  slow, 900 health, rough 0.08 - dirt and grass hardly slow it; art v2 already had its model, the classic view draws it
  in render/farmart.js). The farm-work contract - the co-op's counter ("Farm work: the co-op tractor on the fields") or
  the phone's job list (🚜 Farm work at ...) - issues the co-op's red tractor like a work truck (jobs.js workTruck: the
  ring and arrows until you're in it, no theft, a garage won't keep it, the return bonus after) and points the tracker
  at the end of the nearest row that needs work; each row pays FARM.pay (plough 22, sow 18, harvest 30), FARM.rows rows
  (8) finish it with a FARM.bonus ($150). Without the contract a tractor still works the rows, unpaid.
- **On the page** (client/render/farmart.js, loaded the first time the server sends a 'garden' or 'fields' message - the
  page's own code grew by a few lines: main.js's two messages and two draw calls, the bag's icons). The server sends the

  both renderers - the classic world pass after the flora, art v2 as ground decals before the entities (one line in

## 2026-10-11 · Inside your own home: walk in, the rooms, the bed, the wardrobe, the safe, the fridge, the shower, the garage (H62)

The owner: "after the honest jobs are in can we get more of the owning a house features up? Like going inside your own
house would be great to get going." Going inside was standing still at the door, then hidden there behind a menu - no
inside to walk round.
- How: the inside is a little level of its own (shared/homelayout.js), not a cut-away of the building on the map - a plan
  for each kind of home (a trailer for a shack; an apartment; a house - farmhouses, cottages and beach houses too - with
  its garage; a mansion with the great room, the den and a three-car garage), furnished by the home's price (the shack's
  bare floor to the mansion's rugs and plants; four tiers). Why: World v3 will move and reshape the homes, and a plan
  keyed by the kind and the price goes wherever a home ends up; the map isn't touched, so today's world hash doesn't
  change (World v3's code hash `world3` moves, as for any edit of shared/rules.js it imports).
- At your own front door the action button opens it and you're in (wanted but out of sight, the key takes its moment as
  before; seen by the police, no way in). Walls and furniture you can't walk through, doorways between the rooms; the
  server walks you round (server/systems/homeinside.js), the page predicts your steps with the same function, so it
  answers at once. Nobody sees or hurts you in there (you're out of the world's grid, as before).
- Things to use, each an Act prompt where it stands (the thing in reach is outlined): the bed (sleep: the screen goes
  dark and a clock runs on to the morning; you wake rested - full health, no bleeding - and it's your wake-up spot from
  now on, saved; when everyone online is asleep at home the city's night really passes: the clock jumps to 07:00), the
  wardrobe (a new outfit from your wardrobe, the quick change, the mirror), the safe (your stash: things and guns as
  before, and now cash - kept at home through a death or an arrest), the fridge (food from your bag goes in; eat it from
  there), the shower (stops the bleeding, puts out a burn, a little health), the hall table (the home menu: respawn
  point, the bank, the garage list), the garage's key board (a house or a mansion: through the door from the hall, your
  cars parked in the bays - pick one and you drive it out, the door rolling up), and the front door back out (a couple of
  seconds' protection, as ever). The game doesn't track blood or grime on people, so the shower doesn't clean any.
- Drawn on a canvas of its own over the city view - the same over art v2 and the classic renderer (art v2 adds soft
  shadows under the furniture and lamp light at night); the camera frames the whole place when it fits and follows you
  round a big one; the windows show the time of day (and the light falling in by day). client/render/homeview.js is
  loaded the first time you go in (one line in main.js): nothing added to the page's start-up code.
- Numbers in shared/rules.js HOME_IN (pace, reach, the sleep, the shower). Dev: `homein` ({ kind | id, cars, at }) -
  any home yours and you inside it, standing by the bed, the safe...
- A friend: at someone else's door while they're in, the action button knocks (they hear it, with your name); the owner
  lets you in from the hall table, where who's knocking is listed. You see each other in there (each with a name over
  them; asleep, beside you in the bed), the things are the owner's (the prompt says so), and a guest goes out by the
  front door - or is put out if the place is sold.
- Not done: the cars in the garage's bays aren't solid (you walk through them); a crew of your own to let in without a
  knock (there's no crew in the game yet).

## 2026-10-11 · Owning a home: the real-estate app, a look round before you buy, apartment blocks of homes, a mortgage (H65)

The owner: "can we get more of the owning a house features up?" There was buying and selling at the door, the garage,
waking at home, the home menu and (H62) walking round the inside of your own. Now, in the order asked:
- **The real-estate app on the phone** (🏠 Homes; server/systems/realestate.js works the list out, client/realestate.js
  draws it - loaded when the app opens, the page's start-up code only gains its button and one message line). The homes
  for sale, nearest / cheapest / priciest, all / apartments / houses / big / under $15k (30 at a time): each with a picture
  of its plan (the rooms from above, made from shared/homelayout.js), its district and how well-to-do that is (upscale,
  middling, modest, rough end), the kind (studio, apartment, penthouse, house, cottage...), the unit and floor in a block,
  bedrooms, parking or garage spaces, the yard's garden plots (H61), a boathouse, the price and a mortgage's deposit; tap
  one for a waypoint. Your own homes above them with what they're worth, what selling brings and what's owed.
- **A look round before you buy** (homeinside.js tour): at a home for sale its menu (or a block's lobby) has "Take a look
  inside" - you walk its rooms as a visitor (the things are to look at: "The bed comes with the place"), the price under
  the view, and at the front door a menu: buy it, buy it with a mortgage, step outside, keep looking. Bought from inside,
  it's yours where you stand (the bed, the safe... work at once). Not while wanted; someone else buys it while you're
  looking and you're shown out. A visitor's Act just inside the door is the door, not the hall table beside it.
- **Apartment blocks with several homes** (homes.js buildUnits; HO5): each of the city's apartment blocks (a map home of
  kind 'apartment') is a building of 4 to 8 homes by its footprint, three doors a landing: the map's own home is unit 1
  (the ground floor - whoever owns it keeps it), units 2.. are homes of their own found from the built map when the
  server starts - nothing is added to the map, so the world's hash and signature don't change, and each unit is keyed by
  its building's home (id UNIT0 + the building's home id x 16 + its number), never by where it stands, so World v3 can
  move the buildings. A unit is a home like any other (profile.homes and deeds, the respawn point, garage space, the
  inside, the bed, the safe), its plan by its place in the building: a studio (new plan), an apartment a floor up, the
  penthouse at the top (new plan: two bedrooms and a den), each furnished by its price. The lobby door lists them: yours
  to go in, for sale to look round or buy, someone else's to knock at while they're in; your cars come out at the parking
  out front. Several players own homes in one building, each going into their own. On today's world: 25 blocks, 127 new
  homes (166 on the map: 293 homes in all).
- **A mortgage** (mortgage.js; shared/rules.js MORTGAGE): buy for a 20% deposit and the bank lends the rest plus 10%,
  paid back in 10 payments from your bank account, one each in-game day you're in the city (a day away isn't charged).
  A payment the bank can't cover is missed (you're told how many more before...); a third in a row and the bank takes
  the home back (what you paid stays with the bank; your cars and stash are yours). Selling a mortgaged home pays off
  what's owed first. At most 3 at once. profile.loans (absent on older profiles - they load as before; store.js's new
  profiles start with it empty); a world rebuild clears it and buys the home back at what was paid (the deed counts
  the deposit and each payment).
- Files: server/systems/realestate.js, mortgage.js, client/realestate.js (new); homes.js (the units, homeById, homeFor,
  claim / release, a sale paying off a loan), homeinside.js (the tour, a unit's menus from its lobby, knocking from the
  lobby), economy.js (the lobby's list, the tour and mortgage options, the menu's home through homeFor), phone.js (the
  app), shared/homelayout.js (the studio and the penthouse at the end of the plans), shared/rules.js (MORTGAGE at the
  end), world.js (the system), store.js, client/phone.js + main.js (the button, the message), client/hud.js (the menu

- Tests: test/realestate.test.js (the blocks and their units, ids by building, the new plans; the app's listings, sorted

  byte (bit 7 on, the way it points in 32 steps and how far, 0-510 px - the aircraft have no turret there), drawn in both

  touching down softly on the runway, rolling out and stopping (gone once nobody's looking). Only the way along the

## 2026-10-11 · The firefighter and the paramedic: the fire engine, the calls, the hose, grass fires that spread; the ambulance, treating the hurt (H68)

The owner wants "more jobs for players trying to make an honest living" - the brief: the firefighter (and the paramedic
if time allows), now that the game has fire (burning cars and wrecks, people on fire, campfires, explosions) and a fire
engine with a siren.
- **Signing on** (`server/systems/firefighter.js` start, interaction; `phone.js` the job list's 🚒 Firefighter row, take,
  the tracker): Act at a fire station (the map's `Fire Station N` places, found from the built map) or take it from the
  phone: a fire engine is issued like a work truck (`jobs.workTruck` - yours, kept while the job's on, the green ring and
  the arrows, the return bonus after the shift). The H key now works the siren of anything with one (`players.js`:
  `def.siren` as well as `def.police` - the fire engine, the ambulance), so traffic pulls over for it as for the police.
  A shift (`FIRE.shiftS`, 30 minutes, longer with each call answered) of calls, one after another (`FIRE.gapS`).
- **The calls** (`newCall`, `callAt`; places from the built map: `sitesOf` - never coordinates): from `FIRE.minD` to
  `FIRE.maxD` px away -
  - a car on fire at the kerb (a parking spot in town: `v.dead` with its fire lit, `deadBoomAt` 80 s off) - left alone
    it blows (the vehicle's own explosion);
  - a wreck burning after a crash (kept from being tidied away while it burns, `FIRE.wreck.burnS`) - left alone for
    `spreadS` it lights what's beside it: the grass, or a parked car (whose engine dies and catches - another fire);
  - someone on fire outside a shop or at a cookout in a park - they catch as the crew comes within `FIRE.person.nearR`
    (burning.js ignite: they fall and burn) and live `lifeS` s burning;
  - a grass fire in a park or the countryside (open grass in a park / rural / wild district with a road near, not the
    roadless islands);
  - a dumpster on fire behind a shop (the nearest dumpster prop) or a kitchen fire in a cafe, a diner, a store - they
    grow while nobody's at them and, hot enough, light the grass beside them.
- **The tile fires** (`world.tfire`: `light`, `stepFires`; `shared/rules.js FIRE.grass`, `FIRE.spot`): a new kind of
  fire, all on the server and cheap - a map of burning tiles stepped twice a second. A grass tile burns `burnS` (11 s)
  and leaves scorched ground for 15 minutes (no fire there again); each second each burning tile lights a neighbour
  in dry grass (T.GRASS, T.FIELD) with chance `spread` (diagonals less), never more than `max` (200) burning at once
  nor further than `maxR` (14 tiles) from where it started. In the rain it hardly spreads (x0.05) and each tile burns a
  quarter as long - it dies. Walking through it sets you alight (burning.js). Anyone's wreck by the grass can start one.
- **The hose** (`hose`, `spray`, `cool`): on foot within `FIRE.hose.len` (420 px) of your own engine, the fire button is
  the hose, not your weapon (`players.js`: the end of the golf / hoops / bowling list). The water reaches `range` (190
  px; a wall stops it), `w` px either side: it douses anyone on fire (burning.js douse 'water' - a call's victim saved),
  holds a dying car off while it's on it and puts it out after `FIRE.car.douseS` (4 s: the boom and the fire called off
  for good - "saved"), puts out a burning wreck (5 s) or a fire arrow's flames, takes the tile fires' heat down (a grass
  tile 0.6 s, a dumpster 3.5, a kitchen 7 - more once they've grown) and wets the grass where it lands (`wetS`: a wet
  tile won't catch, so a line of water stops the front). Just out of reach of the engine, it says so (and no punch
  comes out); well away from it, the fire button is your weapon as ever. Nothing up in the air above FLY.HIGH is touched.
  A job given up or a player gone mid-call: the call's car goes back to the traffic's books, someone waiting for the
  crew is gone (`letGo`, every second; the paramedic's patient too).
- **The pay** (`endCall`; `FIRE.pay`): the call's base by kind ($150-280), up to +50% for a fire out quickly (against
  a par of 60 s plus a second per 600 px of the drive), +$150 for a car saved from blowing up, +$200 for a life saved;
  a grass fire $4 less a tile it burned (down to a third); a Samaritan point a call. A car that blew, someone who died,
  a call left `callS` (5 minutes): unpaid. The engine lost: off the crew.
- **Seen and heard** (`client/render/firejob.js`, new, lazy: loaded the first time a fire or a hose is near you): the
  server sends `{ t: 'fires', f: [tx, ty, kind, heat...], s: [scorched tiles] }` within `FIRE.near` of you when it
  changes, and a `hose` event (who, where, the angle, the reach, the engine) every other tick while one sprays. Drawn on
  the overlay both renderers share (main.js drawOverlays: over the classic world, on the layer over art v2's) so it's
  the same in both: the scorched grass (dark, blotched, ash-flecked), the flames (pre-drawn tongues, four frames,
  flickering; a dumpster's or a kitchen's taller) over a glow, smoke rising (the pooled particles), the red hose from the
  engine to the firefighter, the water's stream (three layers, wavering) and its spray where it lands. The hose sounds
  ('gush'). main.js grew by the two message lines and the draw call (the page 484 KB of 485).
- The debug menu's 🔥 section (`client/devcats.js`, its end; `dev.js` 'firejob'): a call of each kind beside you, on the
  crew with your engine parked behind you.
- **The paramedic** (`server/systems/paramedic.js`, new; `shared/rules.js MEDIC`): Act at a hospital's doors (its
  `hospital` place on the map) or take it from the phone (🚑 Paramedic): an ambulance is issued (`jobs.workTruck`, its
  siren on H). Calls, one after another, from `MEDIC.minD` to `maxD` px away, by the shops or in the parks
  (firefighter.js `sitesOf` / `openNear`: open ground outdoors): someone who's had a fall (minor - hold Act by them
  `treatS` s and they're up and on their way) or someone badly hurt (serious - treat them to stabilise them; pull the
  ambulance up alongside, stopped, and they're helped aboard; stop by a hospital's doors, within `hospitalR`, and
  they're handed over). The patient lies there (`downUntil`: the down pose; `npc.sar`: npc.js leaves them be). Letting go
  of Act loses the treatment at half the rate. Untreated, a minor patient gives up (`lifeS.minor`), a serious one dies
  (`lifeS.serious`, 150 s); aboard they have `rideS` (180 s) to reach a hospital. A player down within `maxD` comes
  first: revive them (revive.js's own hold-Act revive; `p.giveTo` says it was you). The pay: by kind ($140 / $220 /
  $200), up to +50% for a quick call, + $60 a km from the scene to the hospital; 2 Samaritan points. No new drawing:
  the patient is an NPC lying down, the tracker points at them, then at the nearest hospital. The debug menu: 🚑 a
  patient beside you (`dev.js` 'medicjob').

Playtest (headless, both views; screenshots in the helper's scratchpad `h68/`): the engine at a burning car in Downtown,
the hose on it (the stream from the firefighter to the car, the hose line back to the engine; saved, +$450); a grass fire
in Greenfield Park with its scorched middle and its front, the hose on it; the same in art v2 in Highland Woods. What's

burns (no depth); the classic view's own burning-car flames are small next to the grass fire's; a dumpster behind a

The phone's Jobs app lists them under Emergency services (`client/phone.js`: the flying list's rows, with their own

## 2026-10-11 · Driving for a living: the taxi driver, the bus driver, the tow truck driver (H72)

The owner: "Let's add more jobs for players trying to make an honest living." The brief: a taxi driver, a bus driver
and, time allowing, a tow truck driver - each built on what the city already has (its taxis, its bus lines, its tow
service), all of it on the server, the page only drawing.
- **The taxi driver** (`server/systems/taxijob.js`): sign on at a taxi rank - the rail stations and the airports
  (`ranksOf`, from the built map) - with Act by it, or from the phone's job list (the new 🚕 row under **Driving**): a
  Checker Taxi is issued like a work truck (`jobs.workTruck` - yours, the ring and the arrows, the return bonus after the
  shift). A shift (`CAB.shiftS`, longer with each fare) of fares, one after another: someone at the kerb near you
  hailing a cab (`CAB.hail` px off; drawn with an arm up - the person's prop `pp: 'hail'`, a new pose in art v2's
  people.js) or someone further off who rang for one (on the phone at their ear, `pp: 'call'`); both are marked (the
  job tracker's pick-up stage, with where they're going on the minimap). Stop by them and they walk over and get in
  the back; the meter runs while they're aboard (the tracker reads "meter $N", once a second) and the tracker points
  to where they want to go - a place from the map (`GOES`: shops, banks, clubs, stations, homes...) `CAB.trip` px
  off. Stop at the kerb by it and they get out and pay: the flag fall and the distance (the meter, at most 1.6x the
  straight line - no driving round the block for more), and a tip (`CAB.tip` of the fare at best) for a quick ride
  (the par time by the distance) and a smooth one: each crash (a hard hit - `v.hardHit` over `CAB.bump`) costs half
  of it, anyone hit (the car-hit events: run over, on the hood, flung near the cab) all of it, and the police after you
  (wanted while they're aboard) all of it. Each of those scares them too ("Whoa - easy!"); `CAB.bail` scares and they
  want out - at the next stop they get out and storm off without paying.
- **The bus driver** (`server/systems/busjob.js`): sign on at any stop of a line (Act by its shelter) or from the
  phone (the line nearest you): a City Bus in the line's livery is issued on the line's street just before that stop.
  Drive the loop (`transit.js busLines` - its stops in order; the tracker points to the next stop and says when it's
  due and how many are aboard). People wait at the next stop's shelter (`BUSJOB.wait` of them, each going one to three
  stops on). Pull up at the stop (stopped within `haltR`) and the doors open: whoever's for this stop gets off at the
  shelter, the ones waiting walk to the door on the kerb side and board (each pays the fare, `perPax`; held up getting
  there, they squeeze on after a while), and after `dwellS` with everyone aboard the stop's done: on time (by the
  timetable - the leg at `BUSJOB.speed`, the dwell, `late` s grace) it pays `perStop`, late nothing for the stop. Once
  round the loop the shift's done; cancelled or lost, everyone gets off.
- **The tow truck driver** (`server/systems/towjob.js`): sign on at a police station (its impound lot) or from the
  phone: a Tow Truck is issued. Calls: a wreck or a car broken down in the street that the city's tow service would
  come for (`tow.js towReason` - the city's own trucks leave it to you: `v.towCall`), or with none about a car broken
  down at a kerb somewhere near (smoking, 20% health). Back up to it - stopped, your tail touching either end of it
  (`TOWJOB.touch`, `tow.js tailGap`, exported) - and the winch works `hookS`; it goes up on the wheel lift by that end
  (`v.towedBy`, `v.towEnd`, `v.towFrom`: the same wire byte as the NPC trucks', so the page draws it tilted on the
  hook, winched round) and rides behind the boom (`tow.js carry`, exported; after the physics each tick). Stop within
  `yardR` of the nearest impound and it's paid: `pay` and `perKm` for the distance towed.
- Rules (`shared/rules.js`, kept short - the city worker loads it): `CAB`, `BUSJOB`, `TOWJOB`.
- Hooks, each at the end of its list: `world.js` SYSTEMS (taxijob, busjob, towjob), `players.js` interaction (after
  the paramedic), `phone.js` (the job list's Driving rows, take, the tracker's target), `client/phone.js` (the Driving
  heading), `dev.js` / `client/devcats.js` (a new dev section, 🚕 Taxi, bus & tow truck: a fare hailing by your cab at
  the kerb; you at the wheel of the bus at its next stop; a broken-down car with your truck backed up to it).
- The page: one line in `client/phone.js`, the hail pose in `client/art2/people.js` and `game/peds.js` (a few hundred
  bytes; people.js is in the chunk bake, so the art hash changes and baked chunks are made again once).
- Playtest (headless, the dev menu's scenes): a fare hailing by Downtown Station, marked, gets in - the tracker reads
  "Taxi: a student to First Pixel Bank - Northgate - meter $25" and counts up as you drive; driven like a maniac
  (the headless key held far too long) the fare complains ("Are you trying to kill us?") and wants out, and the hit
  pedestrian brings the police. The Metro Loop bus at Midtown: four waiting got on and paid, the stop on time, the
  tracker on to Downtown 2 with "4 aboard". The tow truck backed up to a broken-down Sedan: hooked, the car up on the
  lift behind the boom, the tracker pointing to the impound. Seen wrong: the headless page draws a vehicle or a person
  that's just been put somewhere many seconds late (the ring with no cab in it); an NPC bus pulling in to the stop by
  the station shoved a car parked at the pavement's edge hundreds of px along (the game's physics, not the jobs - the
  dev scene now parks the cab further from the road); the fare with an arm up is small at the game's zoom.

Tests: test/drivejobs.test.js (new, 7 tests: the taxi on the job list and at a rank, the cab issued and marked; a fare
hailing with an arm up, picked up, the meter running on the tracker, dropped at the kerb and paid by the distance with
a tip; a crash costs part of the tip and the police all of it; three scares and the fare bails out without paying; the
bus issued in the line's livery, the waiting passengers boarding and paying, the ones for a stop getting off there, a
stop on time paid and a late one not, everyone off when the shift's cancelled; the tow truck backed up to a car, hooked
by its nose, riding on the hook to the impound, paid; the dev menu's three scenes), test/phones.test.js,
test/honestliving.test.js, test/paramedic.test.js, test/transit.test.js, test/tow.test.js, test/lazypage.test.js.

## 2026-10-11 · Decorating your home: a furniture counter, place / move / turn / sell back, the walls' paint and the floors (H67)

The owner asked for "more of the owning a house features"; the brief, after the HO4 concept ("Decorate home - make it
yours"): a furniture shop, an edit mode at home, the paint and the floors per room, kept per home. Until now a home's
furniture was its plan's, fixed by the kind and the price.
- **The furniture counter**: the hardware store (Nail & Gear Hardware - a store the map already has, so the world's hash
  doesn't move) has "Furniture & decor for your home" at the top of its menu: a sofa, an armchair, a dining table, a
  bedside table, a floor lamp, a bookshelf, a potted plant, a TV on a stand, a wall TV, a painting, a rug, a washing
  machine, a workbench (prices in shared/rules.js DECOR). You need a home to buy one; it waits in your homes' storage
  (profile.furn) until you place it.
- **Decorate** (the hall table's menu): face a spot and press Act - the spot's menu: place a piece from storage (it
  comes into your hands facing you), and at a piece of yours: move it, turn it, sell it back (DECOR.sellBack: half its
  price, to the wallet), put it in storage; "Paint this room, lay a new floor" (the room you stand in: six wall colours,
  seven floors - planks light / oak / dark, tiles, marble, carpet, plum carpet; DECOR.paint / DECOR.floor each); Done
  decorating. With a piece in your hands the tiles in front of you show where it would go - green where it fits, red
  where it can't, an arrow for the way it faces - and Act's menu puts it down, turns it, puts it back, or ends.
- **The house rules** (shared/homedecor.js canPlace - the server's word, the page shows the same): a standing piece only
  on open floor (not a doorway, a wall, the tile inside the front door, a garage bay); never cutting off a spot you
  could walk to before, the front door or anything you use (the bed, the wardrobe, the safe, the fridge, the shower,
  the hall table, the garage's key board) - "That would block the bed" etc.; never on someone standing there. A rug
  lies on the floor (furniture stands on it); a painting or a wall TV hangs on a plain wall behind it (not a window, not
  the cut front walls). At most DECOR.max pieces in a home.
- **Kept per home**: profile.decor[home id] { it: placed pieces { k, tx, ty, r }, wall: { room: colour }, floor: { room:
  floor } } (absent on older profiles: they load as before). Sold or taken back by the bank, or the world rebuilt under
  it: the pieces go back into storage for the next home. A guest sees the owner's decor. The rooms are the plan's open
  tiles between the walls, numbered as client/render/homeart2.js numbers them, so the paint goes where it's drawn.
- How: a plan stays as it was (shared/homelayout.js); shared/homedecor.js `decorate(plan, decor)` lays a home's things over
  it - the same layout with your pieces in its list and solid where they stand - and the server walks you round it
  (homeinside.js planIn), the page predicts your steps on the same one. A change replaces the decor object, so the page's
  drawing is made again (art v2: a little a frame, the classic drawing meanwhile).
- **Drawn in both views**: art v2 - the shop's new pieces as voxel models (client/art2/props-home.js: a bedside table with
  its lamp, a floor lamp, a wall TV, a painting, a washing machine, a workbench with its pegboard; the sofa, armchair,
  table, bookshelf, plant and TV are the plans' own models), each turned the way you set it, the lamps and the wall TV
  lit at night, the rugs woven into the floor, the painted walls and the new floors; the classic view - flat sprites for
  the new pieces, the walls' faces painted, the floors by the room's choice, the lamps glowing at night. The page's
  start-up code only gains a line in hud.js (the menu closes as you pick a piece up or put it down); everything else
  is in the lazily loaded home code (homeview.js, homeart2.js, props-home.js, shared/homedecor.js) and DECOR in rules.js
  (the prices only: a line, but rules.js is in every part - the page stays 483 of 485 KB, the city worker 357 of 360
  and the bake 759 of 765, each up 1 KB or less).
- Dev: `decor` (inside a home of yours): { furn: n of every piece into storage, demo: a house's rooms furnished, wall /
  floor: { room: choice }, edit: a kind in your hands (false: done), at: [tx, ty, a] stand there }.

## 2026-10-11 · The HUD on every screen: the prompt, the notes and the job line never under a button (H70)

The owner's brief: "the HUD on every screen - nothing important hidden". H69's QA sweep found the Act prompt (which
now says what you're about to do - "Steal the Sedan - Vehicle theft", "Get in the Fire Engine - issued to you for the
job") under the round buttons on a phone held sideways (844x390: its first word or two showing), the same on a desktop
at 1280x720 with a long prompt (H68's `hose-grass-v2town.png`), and the notes over the job line on a phone (H69's
`p1-coast.png`). Measured before: 623 overlaps over 72 cases (six sizes, keyboard / pad / touch, on foot / driving /
flying / as the police); after: none.
- **Two columns** (`index.html`, `client/style.css`): the prompt and the notes now share one, `#hud-msg`, right of the
  minimap and under the round buttons (top 50 / 48 px): a prompt that wraps pushes the notes down instead of running
  under them, and nothing in it reaches the round buttons. The job line and the police cruiser's hint share another,
  `#hud-sub`, at the bottom centre (the hint over the job line, pushed up when the job line wraps).
- **On touch** the job line sits at the bottom between the sticks (left of the horn / descend / brake buttons, right of
  the left stick - `right: +316px` from the safe area); the prompt and notes column runs from the ITEMS / flashlight
  buttons to just short of the cash (`min(380px, 100vw - 482px)`). H69's idea - the prompt on the right under the cash,
  just above ACT - measured short: under the cash there's 62 px above CAR at 844x390 and 37 px at 740x360, one line of a
  prompt that runs to three, so it stays on the left where it can wrap.
- **Phones on their side** (`@media (max-height: 430px)`): the faction (CITIZEN, POLICE · SERGEANT) gets a row of its own
  under the stars, so the cash and the stars take less width and the prompt has room beside them; the job line 13 px.
  While there's a prompt (or a bar), the newest note only, so the column ends above you in the middle of the screen
  (the first try ran a three-line prompt and two notes down to your feet). Under 380 px tall (740x360, an iPhone in
  Safari) one note at a time always and a 13 px prompt. At 740 px wide the round
  buttons are 30 px (they ran under the weapon plate) and the police's COP CAR button sits under the minimap (it lay over
  the menu button).
- **A keyboard or a pad on a short screen** (a phone with a keyboard, a short window; the touch controls go when a key
  is pressed): the round buttons beside the minimap, the column clear of the weapon, two notes at a time, the job line
  lower. Upright with a keyboard (a narrow desktop window) the column goes under the minimap.
- **The prompt's colour for a crime**: there was none yet - now what Act would do as a crime puts the prompt's plate
  edge and words in amber, a felony in red (`server/systems/players.js`: the act's `crime` goes to the page as `me.pcr`,
  1 or 2; `client/hud.js` `.crime` / `.felony`).
- **The robbery, train and custody bars** (`#rob`, `#trainbar`) head the same column, over the prompt (they sat at top
  118 centred, across the prompt and the notes on every screen but 1920; the custody bar low down over a wrapped job
  line and, on a phone, over FIRE and RELOAD). A phone upright keeps them in the middle as before. On a phone on its side
  with a bar showing, the newest note only; at 740 px the robbery bar drops its ROBBERY label (the gold edge says it) to
  stay on one line.
- **The spectator's notes** still show alone, bottom right (the column is let go of while spectating).
- **Menus**: a row whose label and note run long puts the note on a line of its own (`hud.js` `.opt.two`) - the
  lobby's "Unit 1 for sale - look round or buy" wrapped "buy" into the start of "apartment, ground floor · 1 bed".
- **Decorating**: a piece that would cut most of the home off from the front door now says "That would cut the rest of
  the home off from the front door - leave a way through" instead of naming the first thing in there it would block
  (H67's sofa across the hall said "the shower") - when more than half of where you could walk is lost
  (`shared/homedecor.js` canPlace). A piece that shuts one room still names what's in it (the trailer's bed).

**The test** (`test/hudlayout.test.js`, `test/hudpage.js`): index.html's HUD and touch controls with the stylesheet, no
game code, filled with the longest prompt, four long notes, a long job line and the cruiser's hint, big cash and bank,

## 2026-10-11 · Owning a home, the small things: the lobby you walk into, the mail, the doorbell, a pet at home, a quicker redraw (H71)

The owner asked for "more of the owning a house features"; the brief, after the HO5 (apartment buildings) and HO3 (life

decor that doesn't redraw the whole room (H67 saw several seconds).
- **The lobby** (shared/homelayout.js lobby4 .. lobby8, by the block's number of flats; server/systems/homeinside.js):
  an apartment block's front door opens into its lobby - anyone may walk in, a shared, safe place out of the world like a
  home (nobody sees or hurts you in there; the police can't follow you in while they see you, and wanted but out of
  sight the door takes its moment, as a home's). The tiled hall: the mailboxes on the back wall, the lift beside them,
  the stairs up in the corner, a plant by the door; the landing's red runner along the back wall with a numbered door
  for each flat (unit 1 first). At a door: yours - go in; one for sale - its menu: look round, buy it, buy it with a
  mortgage (bought, you're in); someone else's - ring their doorbell while they're in (nobody in: it says whose). Out of
  a flat's front door - yours, a look round, a friend's - you're back on the landing outside it; the lobby's own door
  is the street. Two players in the lobby see each other. Nothing is added to the map: the lobby is a place of its own
  keyed by its building (homes.js world.lobbies, id unit 0's), so the world's hash doesn't move. Your cars still come
  out at the parking out front - from your flat's hall table (its garage list), as before.

(after the blast), FA5 (garden plots by stage), FA4 (tractors and the fields), MV1 (the tank and the attack helicopter).

  MOVING, DEAD, the swim bit) plus one new bit: **burned to death** (`server/systems/combat.js` kill sets `ped.charred`
  when the cause is fire; `server/net.js` sends it as the parent field's next bit, 0x40000000, under the burn bit;
  `client/main.js` strips both and notes when the burn bit comes on and goes off). `main.js` pedLook: catching (the

  pose); put out but still down: pushing up to get up (downF). burnFx: the flames start at the legs and climb the body
